{{Short description|Statistical area in France}}

[[File:FR-AAV-2020-simplified.png|thumb|upright=1.5|Functional areas (AAV) of [[Metropolitan France]] in 2020, broken down by [[Communes of France|communes]] (commune borders as of January 1, 2020):
{{legend-table|lang=en|title=
|#f23f00|Communes in the main population and employment centre of a functional area
|#fc8054|Communes in a secondary population and employment centre of a functional area
|#ffa600|Communes  in the commuting zone of a functional area (functional areas with more than 700,000 inhabitants)
|#fffa20|Communes  in the commuting zone of a functional area (functional areas between 200,000 and 700,000 inhabitants)
|#d5ef88|Communes  in the commuting zone of a functional area (functional areas between 50,000 and 200,000 inhabitants)
|#fbeea8|Communes  in the commuting zone of a functional area (functional areas with less than 50,000 inhabitants)
|#ffffff|Communes outside of functional areas
}}]]

An '''''aire d'attraction d'une ville'''''{{refn|Plural: ''aires d'attraction des villes''.<ref name=AAV>{{cite web |url=https://www.insee.fr/fr/information/4808607 |title=Le nouveau zonage en aires d'attraction des villes |publisher=[[Institut national de la statistique et des études économiques|INSEE]]|access-date=2022-04-26}}</ref>|group=note}} (or '''AAV''', literally meaning "catchment area of a city") is a statistical area used by [[France]]'s national statistics office [[Institut national de la statistique et des études économiques|INSEE]] since 2020, officially translated as '''functional area''' in English by INSEE,<ref name=FU>{{cite web |url=https://www.insee.fr/en/metadonnees/definition/c2173 |title=Functional areas - Definition |publisher=[[Institut national de la statistique et des études économiques|INSEE]]|access-date=2022-04-26}}</ref> which consists of a densely populated [[urban area|urban agglomeration]] and the surrounding [[exurb]]s, towns and intervening rural areas that are socioeconomically tied to the central urban agglomeration, as measured by [[commuting]] patterns.<ref name=AAV /> INSEE's functional area (AAV) is therefore akin to what is most often called [[metropolitan area]] in English.

==Definition==
INSEE's AAV follows the same definition as the [[larger urban zone|Functional Urban Area]] (FUA) used by [[Eurostat]] and the [[OECD]], and the AAVs are thus strictly comparable to the FUAs.<ref name=FU /> Before 2020, INSEE used another metropolitan statistical area, the ''[[urban area (France)|aire urbaine]]'' (AU), which was defined differently than the AAV, but the AU has now been discontinued and replaced with the AAV in order to facilitate international comparisons with Eurostat's FUAs.<ref name=FU />

The functional area is a grouping of [[Communes of France|communes]] comprising a 'population and employment centre' (''pôle de population et d'emploi'' in French),<ref name=FU /><ref name=French_definition>{{cite web |url=https://www.insee.fr/fr/metadonnees/definition/c2173 |title=Aire d'attraction des villes - Définition |publisher=[[INSEE]]|access-date=2022-04-26}}</ref> which Eurostat calls "city" or "greater city" (depending on the FUA),<ref name=Eurostat>{{cite web |url=https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/cities/spatial-units |title=What is a city? - Spatial units |publisher=[[Eurostat]]|access-date=2022-04-26}}</ref> defined according to population and employment criteria, and an outlying 'commuting zone' (''couronne'' in French),<ref name=FU /><ref name=French_definition /> which Eurostats calls "commuting zone" in English,<ref name=Eurostat /> like INSEE, but ''zone de navettage'' in French<ref>{{cite web |url=https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/fr/web/cities/spatial-units |title=Qu'est-ce qu'une ville? — Unités spatiales |publisher=[[Eurostat]]|access-date=2022-04-26}}</ref> (unlike INSEE which calls it ''couronne''), in which at least 15% of the working population work in the population and employment centre.<ref name=FU />
